children: The draft revised application more than doubles direct customer rate credits, strengthens workforce commitments, and includes a nearly $5 billion commitment to invest in New Mexico's electric grid

ALBUQUERQUE, N.M., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TXNM Energy, the parent company of PNM, and Blackstone Infrastructure today announced they have filed a motion with the NMPRC seeking authorization to file a revised version of their merger application. The motion included a draft of the revised application that would deliver $300 million in customer and community benefits as part of Blackstone Infrastructure's proposed acquisition of TXNM Energy.

The revised application draft includes $220 million in direct customer rate credits, more than doubling the direct rate credit commitment included in the original application, while expanding commitments to workforce development, economic opportunity, and affordability programs across New Mexico.

"Our focus has been and will continue to be on serving our customers with safe, reliable, affordable energy," said Don Tarry, President and CEO of PNM and TXNM Energy. "These enhanced commitments put real dollars back in customers' pockets, protect the people who do this work every day, and keep PNM locally managed and locally rooted – while giving us the capital to build the grid New Mexico needs."

"This enhanced proposal would deliver unprecedented, tangible benefits directly to customers while helping ensure New Mexico has the resources needed to meet growing energy demand and continue building a reliable, modern electric grid," said Sebastien Sherman and Heidi Boyd, Senior Managing Directors at Blackstone Infrastructure.
The draft revised application includes:
$220 million in direct customer rate credits.
$40 million
for workforce development and economic development initiatives, including job training, scholarships, apprenticeships, and other programs developed in coordination with state and local stakeholders.
$25 million
for virtual power plant technology to create the necessary infrastructure on the utility side of the meter to coordinate customer resources.
$15 million for PNM's Good Neighbor Fund
, quadrupling annual funding for low-income customer assistance.
Enhanced worker protections, including
no involuntary workforce reductions and no cuts to wages or benefits
, continued support for existing labor agreements, and commitments to prioritize local hiring and apprenticeship opportunities.
A commitment to support PNM's nearly $5 billion capital investment plan
, helping the utility meet rising demand, improve reliability, and support New Mexico's long-term energy needs and clean energy goals.
The draft revised application also includes commitments to New Mexico including:
Maintaining PNM and TXNM Energy's headquarters in New Mexico.
Preserving New Mexico-based leadership and management.
Establishing local oversight of economic development funds to support long-term investment in New Mexico.
The proposed transaction remains subject to review and approval by the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission and other customary regulatory approvals.
